text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Heavy fighting rages across Phnomh Penh as forces loyal to rival prime ministers battle for second day running, leaving at least 12 dead amid fears Cambodia sliding towards civil war.

- Singapore government deeply concerned about deterioration of situation in Cambodia and calls on all parties involved to exercise utmost restraint, cease military activities and restore calm to country.
- Some motor workshops working hand in glove with syndicates that cause road mishaps deliberately. They then share profit from repairs and insurance claims.

- Businessman Ramdas Nair granted option to buy 8.08 million shares in Ho Wah Genting International, which if he exercises it will result in him having to make a general takeover offer for SESDAQ-listed company.
- Singapore may be small country, but its government runs world's highest budget surplus.
- Singapore economic growth expected to have picked up to about 6.3 percent in second quarter on the back of slight manufacturing rebound.

- Hong Kong's property sector records robust first half with record 115,673 transactions registered, suggesting developers will be announcing strong half-year results in coming corporate reporting season.

- Authorised car agents cross great divide to do what they have long fought against: parallel importing. At least two sole distributors set up companies to import and retail brands outside their franchise agreements.

- From walkway tiles in housing board estates to concrete that holds Holland Road flyover in place, handiwork of Koh Brothers subsidiary G&W Group, due to list on Stock Exchange of Singapore, evident in major public projects.
- Lim Goh Tong, richest man in Malaysia, will celebrate his 80th birthday next month, but tycoon may not have urge to pop champagne due to dismal share prices of his Genting group of companiues.
